title: The Impact of Education on Chronic Disease Risk

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS), using quarter-of-birth (z) as an instrument for years of education (x).
- Why IV: Education is endogenous (ability, family background, health endowments may affect both education and later-life chronic disease risk). Quarter-of-birth shifts compulsory schooling age via school-entry laws and therefore shifts attained education but is plausibly unrelated to latent determinants of chronic disease risk.
- Key assumptions:
  - Relevance: z affects x (first-stage is strong; test via first-stage F-statistic).
  - Exclusion: z affects chronic disease only through education, not directly (e.g., no seasonal birth effects on health that persist to adulthood beyond what controls capture).
  - Independence: z is as-good-as-random with respect to unobservables affecting y (conditional on controls).
  - Monotonicity: quarter-of-birth shifts education in the same direction for everyone (no defiers).
- Estimand: LATE of an additional year of education on chronic disease risk for compliers with respect to z. We estimate a linear model (LPM) for interpretability; robustness includes LIML.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code

# 0) Setup --------------------------------------------------------------------
required_pkgs <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest", "car")
to_install <- required_pkgs[!sapply(required_pkgs, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(to_install) > 0) {
  install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
library(AER)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(car)

options(digits = 4)

# 1) Load data ----------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s72_data.csv")

# Quick sanity checks
# str(df); summary(df)

# 2) Models -------------------------------------------------------------------
# Naive OLS (with controls)
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = df)
ols_vcov <- vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1")
ols_ct <- coeftest(ols, vcov = ols_vcov)

# First stage: x on z (and controls)
fs <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = df)
fs_vcov <- vcovHC(fs, type = "HC1")

# Robust first-stage F-test for instrument relevance (H0: z = 0)
fs_test <- linearHypothesis(fs, "z = 0", vcov = fs_vcov, test = "F")

# 2SLS main specification: y ~ x + controls | z + controls
iv_2sls <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df, method = "2SLS")
iv_vcov <- vcovHC(iv_2sls, type = "HC1")
iv_ct <- coeftest(iv_2sls, vcov = iv_vcov)

# Diagnostics (classical, not robust): weak instrument F, Wu-Hausman, Durbin
iv_sum_diag <- summary(iv_2sls, diagnostics = TRUE)

# LIML as robustness
iv_liml <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | z + controls, data = df, method = "LIML")
liml_vcov <- vcovHC(iv_liml, type = "HC1")
liml_ct <- coeftest(iv_liml, vcov = liml_vcov)

# Additional robustness: exclude controls
iv_2sls_noc <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df, method = "2SLS")
iv_noc_vcov <- vcovHC(iv_2sls_noc, type = "HC1")
iv_noc_ct <- coeftest(iv_2sls_noc, vcov = iv_noc_vcov)

ols_noc <- lm(y ~ x, data = df)
ols_noc_vcov <- vcovHC(ols_noc, type = "HC1")
ols_noc_ct <- coeftest(ols_noc, vcov = ols_noc_vcov)

# 3) Extract key results ------------------------------------------------------
grab_coef <- function(ct, name = "x") {
  cf <- ct[rownames(ct) == name, , drop = FALSE]
  est <- as.numeric(cf[1,1]); se <- as.numeric(cf[1,2])
  ci_low <- est - 1.96 * se; ci_high <- est + 1.96 * se
  list(est = est, se = se, ci_low = ci_low, ci_high = ci_high)
}

ols_res      <- grab_coef(ols_ct, "x")
iv_res       <- grab_coef(iv_ct, "x")
liml_res     <- grab_coef(liml_ct, "x")
iv_noc_res   <- grab_coef(iv_noc_ct, "x")
ols_noc_res  <- grab_coef(ols_noc_ct, "x")

# Classical (non-robust) first-stage F on excluded instrument from ivreg summary
weakF <- NA
if (!is.null(iv_sum_diag$diagnostics)) {
  if ("Weak instruments" %in% rownames(iv_sum_diag$diagnostics)) {
    weakF <- iv_sum_diag$diagnostics["Weak instruments", "statistic"]
  }
}

# 4) Print results ------------------------------------------------------------
cat("Sample size:", nrow(df), "\n\n")

cat("Naive OLS (with controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef on education (x): %0.4f  [SE_robust = %0.4f]  95%% CI: [%0.4f, %0.4f]\n\n",
            ols_res$est, ols_res$se, ols_res$ci_low, ols_res$ci_high))

cat("IV 2SLS (main, with controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef on education (x): %0.4f  [SE_robust = %0.4f]  95%% CI: [%0.4f, %0.4f]\n",
            iv_res$est, iv_res$se, iv_res$ci_low, iv_res$ci_high))
if (!is.na(weakF)) {
  cat(sprintf("  Classical first-stage weak-instrument F (ivreg diagnostics): %0.2f\n", weakF))
}
cat(sprintf("  Robust first-stage F for z (H0: z=0 in x~z+controls): %0.2f  (p = %0.4f)\n\n",
            as.numeric(fs_test$F[2]), as.numeric(fs_test$`Pr(>F)`[2])))

# Wu-Hausman and Durbin tests for endogeneity (from ivreg diagnostics)
if (!is.null(iv_sum_diag$diagnostics)) {
  dtab <- iv_sum_diag$diagnostics
  rn <- rownames(dtab)
  if ("Wu-Hausman" %in% rn) {
    cat(sprintf("Wu-Hausman endogeneity test:  stat = %0.2f, p = %0.4f\n",
                dtab["Wu-Hausman","statistic"], dtab["Wu-Hausman","p-value"]))
  }
  if ("Durbin" %in% rn) {
    cat(sprintf("Durbin endogeneity test:     stat = %0.2f, p = %0.4f\n\n",
                dtab["Durbin","statistic"], dtab["Durbin","p-value"]))
  }
}

cat("LIML (with controls) robustness:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef on education (x): %0.4f  [SE_robust = %0.4f]  95%% CI: [%0.4f, %0.4f]\n\n",
            liml_res$est, liml_res$se, liml_res$ci_low, liml_res$ci_high))

cat("Robustness: excluding controls\n")
cat(sprintf("  OLS (no controls):     beta = %0.4f  [SE_robust = %0.4f]  95%% CI: [%0.4f, %0.4f]\n",
            ols_noc_res$est, ols_noc_res$se, ols_noc_res$ci_low, ols_noc_res$ci_high))
cat(sprintf("  IV 2SLS (no controls): beta = %0.4f  [SE_robust = %0.4f]  95%% CI: [%0.4f, %0.4f]\n",
            iv_noc_res$est, iv_noc_res$se, iv_noc_res$ci_low, iv_noc_res$ci_high))

# 5) Clear numerical headline result -----------------------------------------
cat("\nHeadline causal estimate (IV 2SLS with controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("  dY/dEducation = %0.4f  (SE_robust = %0.4f)\n", iv_res$est, iv_res$se))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. More education should reduce chronic disease risk via higher health knowledge, incomes, and healthier behaviors.
- Magnitude: For a binary/near-binary outcome, prior work often finds 1 additional year of schooling lowers chronic disease or poor health by about 1–3 percentage points. If y is standardized (as the preview suggests), expect roughly −0.02 to −0.08 SD per additional year. Robustness may widen CIs given a single binary instrument.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Quarter-of-birth serves as an instrument for education.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Higher educational attainment significantly reduces the risk of chronic diseases.
